desc_decadas: Our archive has no temporal limits...
info_titulo: About the archive content and our criteria
info_p1: This platform features an archive specialized in original Visual Kei and J-Rock audiovisual material, covering physical formats such as DVDs, Blu-rays, and VHS (VHS tapes are fully ripped for digitalization). Our main goal is the rigorous preservation of the technical, artistic, and visual quality of each release, ensuring the content reaches fans exactly as originally conceived by the artists and their respective record labels in Japan.
info_p2: Have you noticed that some of your DVDs or materials do not contain a main menu? This is completely normal. Within the Japanese record industry, if a disc or material includes only a specific music video, a behind-the-scenes making-of, or exclusive commentary, it is extremely common for it to lack an interactive menu. These editions are factory-designed for direct, automatic playback (autorun mode), maintaining a minimalist, distraction-free aesthetic typical of the Japanese physical market.
politica_p1: To maintain an extremely high standard of quality and exclusivity in our catalog, not just any edition is archived. Special releases are exclusively incorporated under two very strict premises, and remember that the photo shown in each post represents the exact edition you will download:
politica_item1_titulo: Made-to-order / Request Limited Editions (完全受注生産限定盤)
politica_item1_desc: Exclusive materials manufactured only according to the exact number of pre-orders requested by fans.
politica_item2_desc: Special initial release versions containing collectibles, alternate covers, or bonus discs, essential for collectors.
politica_footer: In this way, we ensure a curated space focused on pieces of true historical and collectible value for this music genre community.
guia_titulo: Playback Guide for Digitized DVDs, Blu-rays, and VHS
guia_sub: Follow these simple steps to enjoy your audiovisual material correctly according to its intended use:
guia_paso1_t: Download your DVD, Blu-ray, or VHS
guia_paso1_d: Make sure you have enough storage space on your device and that you have downloaded the compressed file or folder with the original structure (such as VIDEO_TS folders in DVDs or BDMV in Blu-rays).
guia_paso2_t: Are you going to burn it to a physical disc?
guia_paso2_d: If you plan to transfer it to a blank/clean DVD or Blu-ray to play it on a traditional home player, skip all further steps and use video-structure-compatible burning software (like ImgBurn or Nero) to burn the image directly.
guia_paso3_d: If you are going to keep it stored on your External Hard Drive or directly on your PC for software playback, proceed to the next step.
guia_paso4_d: Once you have the file ready, use a compatible media player (such as VLC Media Player or MPC-HC). Follow these steps depending on the format:
guia_sub_dvd_d: For folder-structured DVDs or individual VHS videos, you can simply drag the folder or file directly into the player (or use the open file/folder option).
guia_sub_bluray_d: Go to the top menu in Media, click Open Disc, select the Blu-ray option, and browse for the container folder in the disc device section. Finally, click Play.
guia_sub_mpchc_d: Go to File > Quick Open File... or Open Directory... and select the root folder of the format to automatically read the original contents or menus.
